motivation: The paper aims to solve the inverse problem of reconstructing a full-space Hamiltonian from a given effective Hamiltonian, which is a fundamental question in quantum mechanics but not aligned with the user's interests.
method: The problem is reduced to solving a coupled set of polynomial algebraic equations, and computer-assisted symbolic manipulations are used to find explicit algebraic reconstructions for small matrix sizes.
result: The authors demonstrate that explicit algebraic reconstruction is feasible for not too large matrix dimensions.
conclusion: The work provides a method for solving the inverse Feshbach problem, but it is not relevant to the user's research areas.

title: Exact Matching-Polynomial Solution Of The Periodic Baxter-Fendley $z_n$ Clock Chain
authors: Yuguan Li, D. C. Liu, Murray T. Batchelor
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18633v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The periodic non-Hermitian Baxter-Fendley [MATH] clock chain has lacked a complete finite-size spectral solution, whereas its open-chain counterpart admits a solution in terms of independent quasienergies. For the periodic model we show that the operator-valued matching polynomial associated with its cyclic Weyl algebra simultaneously generates a set of conserved quantities, including the Hamiltonian, and realizes a cyclic [MATH] Yang-Baxter transfer matrix. Root-of-unity closure yields a finite system of polynomial spectral equations in each charge sector, which reproduces the complete finite-size energy spectrum counted with algebraic multiplicity. As a first application of this result, we show that Newton continuation of these equations provides a practical numerical route to the periodic ground-state energy without enumerating the full spectrum. For homogeneous chains the thermodynamic seam response yields a criterion for boundary-induced criticality; for [MATH] it predicts two reciprocal critical couplings with singular ground-state curvature, in contrast to the single self-dual open boundary critical point.
tldr: This paper provides an exact spectral solution for the periodic Baxter-Fendley Z_N clock chain using matching polynomials and cyclic Yang-Baxter transfer matrices.
motivation: The periodic non-Hermitian Baxter-Fendley clock chain lacked a complete finite-size spectral solution, unlike its open-chain counterpart. The authors aim to fill this gap and explore applications to criticality.
method: The authors show that the operator-valued matching polynomial associated with the cyclic Weyl algebra generates conserved quantities and realizes a cyclic Yang-Baxter transfer matrix. Root-of-unity closure yields a finite system of polynomial spectral equations in each charge sector.
result: The method reproduces the complete finite-size energy spectrum with algebraic multiplicity. Newton continuation provides a practical numerical route to the ground-state energy, and for Z_3 they predict two reciprocal critical couplings with singular ground-state curvature.
conclusion: The work provides a complete spectral solution for the periodic chain and reveals boundary-induced criticality, contrasting with the open-chain case.

title: Nonlinear Maxwell's Equations As A Boundary Value Problem In Multilayer Nanophotonics
authors: Ruizhe Gu, Dingyang Zhang, Wenjing Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18635v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Calculating strong-field, broadband nonlinear phenomena in complex nanophotonic structures remains difficult because it requires simultaneous handling of non-perturbative dynamics, impulsive processes, and structural complexity. Here, we introduce a unified framework that combines the transfer matrix method with an iterative Green's function approach. The linear multilayer response is incorporated as boundary conditions into a nonlinear boundary value problem, which is then solved self-consistently, naturally accommodating broad spectra and arbitrary nonlinearity. The framework is validated with two examples in the transparent and resonant regimes, respectively. The first demonstrates an impulsive spectral modulation in second harmonic generation that is captured only by a full-structure broadband treatment. The second demonstrates the entire dynamical evolution of exciton-polaritons in a pump-probe experiment reproduced by a unified simulation. This framework directly links nanophotonic design with ultrafast nonlinear dynamics.
tldr: This paper presents a computational framework for simulating nonlinear optical phenomena in multilayer nanophotonic structures, combining transfer matrix and Green's function methods.
motivation: To address the difficulty of calculating strong-field, broadband nonlinear effects in complex nanophotonic structures, which require simultaneous handling of non-perturbative dynamics, impulsive processes, and structural complexity.
method: The authors introduce a unified framework that integrates the transfer matrix method with an iterative Green's function approach, formulating the problem as a nonlinear boundary value problem solved self-consistently.
result: The framework is validated with two examples: one showing impulsive spectral modulation in second harmonic generation, and another reproducing the dynamical evolution of exciton-polaritons in a pump-probe experiment.
conclusion: The framework provides a direct link between nanophotonic design and ultrafast nonlinear dynamics, enabling full-structure broadband simulations.

title: Quantum-Logic Tsetlin Machines: Interpretable Quantum Machine Learning With Commuting Projector Clauses
authors: Krishna Bhatia
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18659v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tsetlin Machines (TMs) learn interpretable Boolean clauses using finite-state automata. We introduce the Quantum-Logic Tsetlin Machine (QL-TM), which replaces Boolean literals with quantum propositions represented by projectors while retaining classical include/exclude automata. Clauses are restricted to commuting measurement contexts and activate through the Born probability of their joint projector. We prove an exact reduction to ordinary Boolean TM clauses in diagonal computational-basis contexts and connect Pauli-projector clauses to stabilizer and syndrome semantics. Controlled experiments on Bell states, phase-flip syndromes, randomized 16-class stabilizer tasks, mixed literal pools, context-budget ablations, and finite-shot noise show that correct non-diagonal contexts recover physically meaningful clauses, while diagonal or wrong contexts lose the relevant phase/syndrome information. The context-budget results closely follow the predicted separability ladder 2^(b-k) as true stabilizer generators are removed. The contribution is a controlled bridge between Tsetlin clause learning and quantum logic, not a claim of quantum advantage.
tldr: Introduces a quantum-logic variant of Tsetlin Machines using commuting projector clauses, but without quantum advantage or direct connection to the specified research directions.
motivation: To bridge interpretable classical machine learning (Tsetlin Machines) with quantum logic, potentially enabling quantum-inspired learning of Boolean clauses.
method: Replaces Boolean literals with quantum projectors in commuting contexts, using Born probabilities for clause activation, and proves reduction to classical TMs in diagonal bases.
result: Experiments show that non-diagonal contexts capture phase/syndrome information, while diagonal contexts lose it; context-budget results match theoretical separability predictions.
conclusion: Provides a controlled bridge between Tsetlin clause learning and quantum logic, but does not claim quantum advantage and is not aligned with the core research interests.

title: Seeded Su(1,1) Interferometry For Fourier-domain Optical Coherence Tomography
authors: Alejandra A. Padilla, Valentina Gacha, Daniel F. Urrego, Juan P. Torres
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18750v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate Fourier-domain optical coherence tomography (FD-OCT) based on a seeded SU(1,1) interferometer. Multilayer objects are probed with broadband light centered at 1550nm, while depth-resolved 3D images are reconstructed from photon flux measurements centered at 810nm. We show that, in the low parametric-gain regime, seeding increases the photon flux, enabling volumetric imaging with a spectrometer rather than single-photon detectors. Our analysis further shows that, under the conditions considered, seeding provides a more effective route to sensitivity enhancement than increasing the parametric gain.
tldr: This paper demonstrates Fourier-domain optical coherence tomography using a seeded SU(1,1) interferometer, enhancing sensitivity for volumetric imaging.
motivation: The authors aim to improve the sensitivity of optical coherence tomography, a medical imaging technique, by using quantum-inspired interferometry.
method: They use a seeded SU(1,1) interferometer with broadband light at 1550 nm and detect photon flux at 810 nm, comparing seeding to increasing parametric gain.
result: Seeding increases photon flux in the low-gain regime, enabling imaging with a spectrometer instead of single-photon detectors, and is more effective than increasing gain.
conclusion: Seeded SU(1,1) interferometry offers a practical sensitivity enhancement for FD-OCT, with potential for broader application.

title: Interior Skin Focusing And Directional Mirror Transfer In A Graded non-Hermitian Krawtchouk Network
authors: X. Z. Zhang Y. S. Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18800v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spatially graded nonreciprocity can move skin weight away from a boundary, but it does not generally preserve a real commensurate spectrum or analytically controlled dynamics. We study a finite open Krawtchouk network with oppositely graded directed hoppings. For a broad intermediate range of asymmetries, their local imaginary gauge field changes sign in the bulk, and its accumulated coordinate generates a positive diagonal similarity map whose normalized squared entries form a biased-binomial envelope. The same map converts the open chain into the spin-rotation generator \(2gJ_x\), so the focus and equally spaced spectrum follow from one grading. In this focusing regime, exact right, left, and biorthogonal eigenvectors show that the envelope width and participation number both scale as \(\sqrt N\), identifying a subextensive interior focus. In the physical node basis, spin rotation produces perfect mirror inversion with direction-selective amplification and attenuation whose gains are mutually inverse. The directional Green functions share their poles, while their residues differ by the same similarity ratio. Closing the chain exposes a gauge-invariant imaginary flux, and either exact one-way limit yields an exceptional point of order \(N\). Onsite disorder preserves the directional resolvent ratio, whereas independent hopping disorder breaks the clean analytic Krawtchouk map and degrades commensurability and transfer. The model therefore provides an exactly solvable finite-network framework linking localization geometry and eigenvector nonorthogonality to commensurate spectra and node-resolved directional response.
tldr: This paper studies a non-Hermitian Krawtchouk network with graded nonreciprocity, showing interior skin focusing and directional mirror transfer, but it is not aligned with the user's research interests.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how spatially graded nonreciprocity can move skin weight away from boundaries while preserving real spectra and controllable dynamics, which is a fundamental question in non-Hermitian physics.
method: They analyze a finite open Krawtchouk network with oppositely graded directed hoppings, using a similarity transformation to map the system to a spin-rotation generator, and derive exact eigenvectors and Green functions.
result: They find a subextensive interior focus with envelope width scaling as sqrt(N), perfect mirror inversion with direction-selective amplification, and an exceptional point of order N in one-way limits. Disorder effects are also examined.
conclusion: The model provides an exactly solvable framework for non-Hermitian skin effects and directional response, but it is not directly relevant to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems as defined by the user.

title: Inverse Born Series Based Neural Operators
authors: John C Schotland, Aseel Titi, Jenn-Nan Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18262v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The inverse Born series provides a general perturbative framework for representing nonlinear inverse maps between infinite-dimensional function spaces and has found numerous applications in inverse problems governed by partial differential equations and integral equations. Motivated by its operator-theoretic structure, we develop a systematic framework for constructing neural operators that approximate the operator expansions arising in the inverse Born series. Our approach combines the analytical representation of the inverse Born series with the expressive power of neural operators, yielding data-driven approximations of the nonlinear inverse map while preserving the underlying operator structure. The proposed framework is applicable to a broad class of inverse problems and is presented in a general functional-analytic setting. To demonstrate its practical performance, we consider two representative examples: inverse scattering and the Calder\'on (electrical impedance tomography) problem. Numerical experiments show that the constructed neural operators accurately approximate the inverse Born expansions and produce high-quality reconstructions across a range of test cases. These results indicate that the proposed methodology provides an effective and computationally efficient approach for learning nonlinear inverse operators and suggests a promising direction for integrating classical operator expansions with modern neural operator architectures.
tldr: This paper develops neural operators based on the inverse Born series for solving inverse problems, but it is not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The authors aim to combine classical operator expansions with modern neural operators to efficiently approximate nonlinear inverse maps in inverse problems.
method: They construct neural operators that mimic the structure of the inverse Born series, using a functional-analytic framework and demonstrate on inverse scattering and Calderón problems.
result: Numerical experiments show accurate approximations and high-quality reconstructions for the tested inverse problems.
conclusion: The proposed methodology offers an effective and computationally efficient approach for learning nonlinear inverse operators, suggesting a promising direction for integrating classical and data-driven methods.

title: Posterior Convergence Without Force Convergence: Resolution-Stable Sampling For Rough Bayesian Inverse Problems
authors: Xiaomei Yang Zhiliang Deng
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18365v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bayesian posteriors can converge under model refinement even when the exact sensitivities used by gradient-based samplers do not. We study this mismatch for discretely scale-invariant rough potentials and its consequences for Metropolized Hamiltonian proposals. For Weierstrass truncations, adjacent classical-force increments grow geometrically in the rough regime, whereas fixed additive quotients converge uniformly and fixed multiplicative quotients converge locally away from the origin. The matched Jackson quotient is distinguished not by convergence alone but by dilation covariance and exact finite closure at the intrinsic scale. Uniform negative-log-likelihood approximation is shown to imply explicit total-variation, Hellinger, and bounded quantity-of-interest convergence, with a Gaussian forward-map criterion for Bayesian inverse problems. At the algorithmic level, measurable kick--drift--kick maps are triangular shears, so exact Metropolis correction does not require differentiability of the proposal field. Local uniform field convergence yields convergence of fixed-length proposals, acceptance functions, and bounded-Lipschitz kernels on common compact sets, while the first classical HMC half-kick has no fixed-step refinement limit. Numerical experiments verify the predicted force-refinement rates, show that posterior stabilization can coexist with severe resolution-dependent retuning of exact-gradient HMC, and demonstrate forward convergence without sensitivity convergence in two-dimensional Darcy flow. The computations are used to assess refinement consistency rather than to claim a universal efficiency ordering among proposal fields.
tldr: This paper studies Bayesian posterior convergence for rough inverse problems, focusing on the mismatch between force convergence and posterior convergence in Hamiltonian Monte Carlo.
motivation: The authors aim to understand when Bayesian posteriors converge under model refinement even if gradient-based samplers' forces do not, which is crucial for reliable uncertainty quantification in rough inverse problems.
method: They analyze discretely scale-invariant rough potentials, compare different finite-difference quotients, and prove convergence of posteriors under uniform likelihood approximation. They also study the algorithmic properties of Metropolized Hamiltonian proposals.
result: They show that posterior convergence can occur without force convergence, and that exact Metropolis correction does not require differentiability of the proposal field. Numerical experiments on Darcy flow confirm the theoretical findings.
conclusion: The paper provides a theoretical framework for understanding posterior convergence in rough Bayesian inverse problems, with implications for the design of sampling algorithms.

title: Joint Beamforming And Phase Shifts Design For RIS-Enabled Rsma-isac Systems
authors: Xuejun Cheng, Qian Zhang, Yuhui Jiao, Yufei Zhao, Zheng Dong, Ju Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18458v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the sensing-centric design of reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-enabled rate-splitting multiple access-integrated sensing and communication (RSMA-ISAC) systems. Specifically, we propose a new beam-gain approximation method to enhance the sensing beam gain while satisfying communication quality-of-service (QoS) constraints.Since the joint optimization of the beamforming vectors and RIS phase shifts is highly coupled and non-convex, existing methods typically rely on generic optimization solvers involving substantial computational complexity. To address this issue, we propose an efficient constraints-separation-based alternating optimization algorithm (CS-AO). Our proposed algorithm effectively decouples the optimization variables and yields closed-form solutions for all subproblems, thereby significantly reducing the computational burden. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm achieves sensing beam-gain performance comparable to successive convex approximation (SCA) and semidefinite relaxation (SDR) benchmarks, while achieving more than 120-fold and 50-fold runtime reductions. In addition, compared with conventional space-division multiple access (SDMA) schemes, the proposed design exhibits substantial sensing beam gain.
tldr: This paper proposes an efficient algorithm for joint beamforming and RIS phase shift optimization in RSMA-ISAC systems, focusing on sensing beam gain under communication QoS constraints.
motivation: The authors aim to reduce computational complexity in optimizing RIS-enabled ISAC systems, which is typically handled by generic solvers with high overhead.
method: They introduce a constraints-separation-based alternating optimization (CS-AO) algorithm that decouples variables and yields closed-form solutions for all subproblems.
result: Simulations show the CS-AO algorithm achieves sensing beam-gain comparable to SCA and SDR benchmarks with over 120-fold and 50-fold runtime reductions, and outperforms SDMA in sensing beam gain.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a computationally efficient solution for sensing-centric RIS-ISAC design, but the work is primarily an engineering optimization study without deep information-theoretic or thermodynamic contributions.

title: A Tutorial On Weight Structure Of Polar Codes
authors: Vlad-Florin Dragoi Mohamamd Rowshan
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This tutorial introduces the algebraic foundations underlying the weight structure of polar codes. Using a monomial-based polynomial formalism, we explain how polar and Reed-Muller codes can be viewed as decreasing monomial codes, enabling systematic characterization and enumeration of low-weight codewords. Its goal is to provide an accessible introduction to affine automorphisms, orbit-based descriptions of minimum and low-weight codewords, and their role in weight enumeration. Through illustrative examples and high-level overviews of recursive and coset-based techniques, the paper aims to prepare readers for deeper engagement with the recent technical literature on the weight distribution of polar codes.
tldr: A tutorial on the algebraic weight structure of polar codes using monomial-based formalism.
motivation: To provide an accessible introduction to the weight distribution of polar codes, which is important for code performance analysis.
method: Uses monomial-based polynomial formalism to describe polar and Reed-Muller codes as decreasing monomial codes, and explains affine automorphisms and orbit-based techniques for weight enumeration.
result: Presents systematic characterization and enumeration of low-weight codewords, with illustrative examples and overviews of recursive and coset-based methods.
conclusion: The tutorial prepares readers for deeper engagement with technical literature on polar code weight distribution.

title: Gcno: Gramian Chebyshev Neural Operator For Physics-Based Compression Of Wireless Channels
authors: Rafid Umayer Murshed, Shahab Hamidi-Rad, Elahe Soltanaghai, Akshay Malhotra
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18522v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large antenna arrays allow wireless systems to serve more users and achieve higher data rates, but they also make channel feedback expensive: the receiving device must repeatedly report a large complex-valued channel matrix to the base station. Most neural compressors treat this matrix like an image and replace it with a fixed-length code that only a matched neural decoder can interpret. The message therefore does not adapt to channel complexity, and changing the antenna count typically requires retraining. We ask whether a device can instead report only the few dominant propagation paths underlying each channel. We introduce the Gramian Chebyshev Neural Operator (GCNO), a physics-based, variable-rate compressor that identifies a sample-dependent set of path directions. GCNO uses receive-transmit channel structure to locate paths, a first-order Taylor correction to refine directions that fall between grid points, and least squares to recover their complex strengths. It is trained without path labels, and the base station reconstructs the channel analytically from the transmitted path tuples rather than through a learned decoder. Across three ray-traced environments, GCNO achieves better reconstruction accuracy at the same payload - or lower payload at the same accuracy - than neural feedback baselines, and transfers to unseen antenna counts without retraining.
tldr: This paper introduces a physics-based neural operator for compressing wireless channel matrices, focusing on efficient feedback in large antenna systems.
motivation: Large antenna arrays require expensive channel feedback; existing neural compressors are inflexible and do not adapt to channel complexity.
method: The Gramian Chebyshev Neural Operator (GCNO) identifies dominant propagation paths using receive-transmit structure, refines directions with Taylor correction, and recovers strengths via least squares, enabling variable-rate compression without path labels.
result: GCNO achieves better reconstruction accuracy at same payload or lower payload at same accuracy compared to neural baselines, and transfers to unseen antenna counts without retraining.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a physics-based, variable-rate channel compression approach that is more efficient and adaptable than existing neural compressors.

title: Constructing Good Abelian Codes Via Shift Bounds And Genetic Algorithms
authors: Cong Yu, Hao Chen, Zhonghua Sun, Shixin Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18664v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the construction of linear codes via abelian codes over finite fields. By exploiting the algebraic structure of multivariate polynomial quotient rings, we derive lower bounds on the minimum distance using a generalized shift bound, which extends the classical van Lint-Wilson bound for cyclic codes. Several infinite families of abelian codes are explicitly constructed, including binary and ternary cases that extend previously known cyclic constructions. To find more abelian codes with good parameters, we apply a genetic algorithm that searches over defining sets represented as binary chromosomes of cyclotomic cosets; the fitness function compares the computed minimum distance against the best known linear code (BKLC) bounds. The search yields multiple record-breaking codes over F_3 and F_4, with improvements over Grassl's tables. Furthermore, the nested structure of these codes enables the application of Construction X, yielding additional linear codes with improved parameters. The results demonstrate that abelian codes, combined with heuristic search, form a viable way for discovering linear codes with unknown parameters.
tldr: This paper constructs good abelian codes over finite fields using shift bounds and genetic algorithms, yielding record-breaking linear codes.
motivation: The authors aim to discover linear codes with unknown parameters by exploiting the algebraic structure of abelian codes and heuristic search.
method: They derive lower bounds on minimum distance via a generalized shift bound, construct infinite families of abelian codes, and apply a genetic algorithm over cyclotomic cosets to search for codes with good parameters.
result: Multiple record-breaking codes over F_3 and F_4 are found, improving on Grassl's tables, and Construction X yields additional codes with improved parameters.
conclusion: Abelian codes combined with heuristic search are a viable method for discovering linear codes with good parameters.

title: Joint Power Allocation And Phase-Shift Design For Beyond-Diagonal Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces-Aided Isac Systems
authors: Yuhui Jiao, Qian Zhang, Xuejun Cheng, Meihui Liu, Jiancheng An, Ju Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18713v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIM) provide an efficient architecture for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) with few radio-frequency (RF) chains. However, diagonal SIM provide only element-wise phase control, so balancing multiuser communication and sensing performance may require additional layers. In this letter, we propose a beyond-diagonal SIM (BD-SIM) architecture for ISAC, enabling controllable intra-layer coupling through reconfigurable impedance networks, thereby enhancing wave-domain processing flexibility. We develop a unified alternating optimization framework applicable to fully-connected, group-connected, and diagonal SIM architectures. Within this framework, we derive a closed-form power allocation rule and propose an effective variable separation algorithm for multi-layer phase-shift design. Simulation results show that the proposed BD-SIM achieve a better communication-sensing trade-off and require fewer layers to attain performance comparable to conventional SIM.
tldr: This paper proposes a beyond-diagonal stacked intelligent metasurface (BD-SIM) architecture for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems, focusing on joint power allocation and phase-shift design.
motivation: To improve the communication-sensing trade-off in ISAC systems by enhancing wave-domain processing flexibility through controllable intra-layer coupling in SIM architectures.
method: The authors propose a BD-SIM architecture with reconfigurable impedance networks and develop a unified alternating optimization framework for fully-connected, group-connected, and diagonal SIM. They derive a closed-form power allocation rule and a variable separation algorithm for multi-layer phase-shift design.
result: Simulation results show that BD-SIM achieves a better communication-sensing trade-off and requires fewer layers to attain performance comparable to conventional SIM.
conclusion: The proposed BD-SIM architecture offers a promising approach for efficient ISAC systems, but the work is primarily focused on wireless communications and metasurface engineering, with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, or quantum networks.

title: Vqc-zti: Variational Quantum Control For Zero Trust Protection Of The Tactile Internet
authors: Mubassir Serneabat Sudipto (iowa State University), Shakil Ahmed (grand Valley State University), Ashfaq Khokhar
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18572v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tactile Internet services couple cyber events directly to physical actuation, so security decisions must improve risk discrimination without perturbing the control path. This paper presents VQC-ZTI, a split-plane Variational Quantum Classifier framework for zero-trust protection of Tactile Internet services, in which an off-path VQC analyzes encrypted-flow telemetry while an on-path policy engine applies cached deterministic grant, restrict, step-up, and deny actions. By decoupling anomaly scoring from enforcement, VQC-ZTI preserves predictable control behavior and allows detector sensitivity and policy aggressiveness to be tuned independently. We evaluate the framework on CESNET-derived aggregated traffic using random, entity-group, and temporal holdouts with a hybrid PyTorch-PennyLane implementation. The full-hybrid Quantum Neural Network achieves mean areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.9981, 0.9974, and 0.9941 and reduces the false-positive rate relative to ExtraTrees by 44.6%, 49.6%, and 67.9%, respectively. A representative component-timing decomposition further illustrates that batched VQC scoring remains in the asynchronous evidence path rather than the immediate enforcement path.
tldr: This paper applies a variational quantum classifier to zero-trust security for Tactile Internet, but it is an applied machine learning paper with no direct connection to the user's core research areas.
motivation: Tactile Internet services require security decisions that do not perturb control paths, motivating a split-plane approach using quantum machine learning for anomaly detection.
method: The authors propose VQC-ZTI, a split-plane framework where an off-path variational quantum classifier analyzes encrypted-flow telemetry, and an on-path policy engine applies cached actions. They implement a hybrid PyTorch-PennyLane QNN and evaluate on CESNET-derived traffic with random, entity-group, and temporal holdouts.
result: The full-hybrid QNN achieves mean AUCs of 0.9981, 0.9974, and 0.9941, reducing false-positive rates by 44.6-67.9% compared to ExtraTrees, with batched VQC scoring in the asynchronous path.
conclusion: The framework demonstrates that quantum machine learning can enhance zero-trust security for Tactile Internet, but the contribution is primarily in applied ML and network security, not in the user's specified research directions.

title: IriSig-Spoof: A Real-World Benchmark For Time-Robust Satellite Rf Fingerprinting And Spoofing Detection
authors: Shichang Guo, Yuanyu Zhang, Shuangrui Zhao, Ji He, Pinchang Zhang, Yulong Shen
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18642v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite Internet is becoming critical communications infrastructure, yet its open wireless links remain vulnerable to satellite impersonation and signal spoofing. Radio frequency fingerprinting (RFF) offers a potential defense by exploiting transmitter-specific hardware imperfections manifested in received signals. However, the reliability of existing satellite RFF methods remains difficult to assess because no unified dataset and benchmark support temporal, open-set, and cross-scenario evaluation. To address this gap, we introduce IriSig-Spoof, a real-world Iridium dataset comprising 5.17 million messages collected from 66 satellites over 32 days, together with software-defined radio (SDR)-generated spoofing signals from indoor and outdoor settings. We further establish three benchmark tasks: temporal robustness evaluation, open-set RFF identification with unknown-signal rejection, and cross-scenario spoofing detection. Experiments using a multi-scale attention convolutional neural network (MACNN) show that temporal robustness varies across configurations, with the best configuration achieving 97.75% average cross-day accuracy. In open-set evaluation, MACNN achieves an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.9715, while showing that effective unknown-signal rejection does not necessarily ensure reliable identity assignment. Cross-scenario experiments reveal differences at low false-positive rates. IriSig-Spoof provides a reproducible basis for evaluating robust RFF methods under temporal variation and changing attack conditions.
tldr: This paper introduces a real-world benchmark for satellite RF fingerprinting and spoofing detection, focusing on temporal robustness and open-set identification.
motivation: Existing satellite RFF methods lack unified datasets and benchmarks for temporal, open-set, and cross-scenario evaluation, hindering reliability assessment.
method: The authors collect 5.17 million Iridium messages from 66 satellites over 32 days and generate SDR-based spoofing signals. They define three benchmark tasks and evaluate a multi-scale attention CNN (MACNN) on them.
result: MACNN achieves 97.75% average cross-day accuracy in the best configuration, an AUROC of 0.9715 for open-set rejection, and reveals differences in cross-scenario detection at low false-positive rates.
conclusion: The benchmark provides a reproducible basis for evaluating robust RFF methods under temporal variation and changing attack conditions, but the work is primarily an applied dataset and benchmark, not aligned with the user's theoretical quantum information interests.

title: Improving LLM-Based Ssh Honeypots Through Prompting And Fine-Tuning
authors: Muris Sladi\'c, Veronica Valeros, Eman Alibali\'c, Sebastian Garcia
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM-based SSH honeypots often use closed cloud LLMs because they give strong shell realism, but cloud models create deployment problems. These include no stable versioning, provider-side changes, attacker-driven cost, and model decommissioning. Local open-weight models avoid these problems, but they usually perform worse and make mistakes that reveal the honeypot. These mistakes include malformed outputs, command echoing, inconsistent filesystem state, and AI-style artifacts. This paper studies how to improve and evaluate the shell emulation accuracy of local LLM-based SSH honeypots using prompt design and supervised fine-tuning. We fine-tune and evaluate eight models in total: the original fine-tuned GPT-3.5 model used in shelLM and seven open-weight local models, each compared to its base model. We also test how prompt structure transfers across model families. Using 34 automated unit tests that measure shell emulation accuracy in single-session and fresh-session settings, we find that prompt design has a large effect and that fine-tuning depends on dataset coverage. Fine-tuning on the original 112-conversation dataset does not improve aggregate pass rate, while an expanded dataset built from honeypot logs produces clearly stronger local models. Taken together, the results suggest that prompting and fine-tuning can each improve local LLM honeypots on their own, but their effects do not combine straightforwardly, since strong rule-based prompting and supervised adaptation can also conflict by addressing overlapping shell-behavior constraints.
tldr: This paper studies improving local LLM-based SSH honeypots via prompting and fine-tuning, which is unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
motivation: The user's research interests focus on quantum information theory, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum systems. This paper is about cybersecurity and machine learning, specifically honeypot emulation, which has no connection to quantum topics.
method: The authors fine-tune and evaluate eight LLM models (including GPT-3.5 and open-weight models) for shell emulation accuracy, using prompt design and supervised fine-tuning, and test with 34 automated unit tests.
result: Prompt design significantly affects performance, fine-tuning depends on dataset coverage, and the effects of prompting and fine-tuning do not combine straightforwardly.
conclusion: The paper concludes that both prompting and fine-tuning can improve local LLM honeypots, but their interaction is complex and requires careful consideration.

title: Integrated Sensing And Communications Over Hierarchical Cellular And Cell-Free Mimo Systems
authors: Hans D. Schotten Wei Jiang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18873v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) over a hybrid system that seamlessly combines legacy cellular base stations with distributed cell-free (CF) access points (APs). We propose a hierarchical ISAC architecture where a central base station (CBS) serves its near users and simultaneously operates as a monostatic radar for aerial target detection, while distributed APs---many idle under user-centric clustering---act as cost-free bistatic receivers. The CBS jointly handles communication processing and multi-static sensing fusion, reducing fronthaul overhead compared to conventional cell-free ISAC. To achieve this, a five-phase time-division duplexing workflow with precise ISAC role assignment is specified. Closed-form expressions for spectral efficiency and multi-static sensing signal-to-noise ratio analytically characterize the communications--sensing Pareto frontier. Numerical results confirm that the proposed hierarchical design simultaneously achieves higher sum throughput and superior sensing accuracy than conventional cell-free ISAC.
tldr: This paper proposes a hierarchical integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) architecture combining cellular and cell-free MIMO systems, focusing on spectral efficiency and sensing accuracy.
motivation: The authors aim to improve ISAC performance by leveraging idle distributed access points as bistatic receivers, reducing fronthaul overhead compared to conventional cell-free ISAC.
method: They design a five-phase TDD workflow with role assignment, derive closed-form expressions for spectral efficiency and sensing SNR, and analyze the Pareto frontier.
result: Numerical results show the hierarchical design achieves higher sum throughput and superior sensing accuracy than conventional cell-free ISAC.
conclusion: The proposed hierarchical ISAC architecture offers a promising trade-off between communication and sensing performance.

title: New Constructions Of Additive Mds Trs Codes
authors: Anuj Kumar Bhagat, Ankit Yadav, Ritumoni Sarma
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18904v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Additive codes over finite fields generalize linear codes, and additive MDS codes provide a natural extension of linear MDS codes. In this article, we study additive twisted Reed--Solomon (TRS) codes and obtain new constructions of additive MDS codes. First, for additive TRS codes with twist [MATH] and an arbitrary hook, we establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the codes to be additive MDS, thereby generalizing the results in Section 3 of [Jiayu Ma et al., New families of additive non-Reed-Solomon MDS codes]. In particular, we show that the existence of an additive MDS TRS code with [MATH] and hook [MATH] yields codes of larger lengths than those obtained for [MATH] and [MATH] in [Jiayu Ma et al., New families of additive non-Reed-Solomon MDS codes]. Next, we consider additive TRS codes with twist vector [MATH] and hook vector [MATH], and derive necessary and sufficient conditions for them to be additive MDS. We further establish the existence of such codes. Using the Schur square technique, we obtain mild conditions under which the constructed families are inequivalent to additive Reed--Solomon (RS) codes. Finally, we determine parity-check matrices for both families of additive MDS codes considered in this article.
tldr: This paper constructs new families of additive MDS twisted Reed-Solomon codes over finite fields.
motivation: The authors aim to extend the theory of additive MDS codes, which generalize linear MDS codes, by studying twisted Reed-Solomon codes with more general parameters.
method: They derive necessary and sufficient conditions for additive TRS codes to be MDS, using algebraic techniques and the Schur square method to prove inequivalence to additive RS codes.
result: They obtain new constructions of additive MDS codes with larger lengths than previously known, and provide parity-check matrices for these codes.
conclusion: The work contributes to classical coding theory, but it is not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: FedGuard-DC: Privacy-Preserving Federated Load Forecasting And Cyber-Attack Detection For Data-Center Loads In Transmission Systems
authors: Md Rubel Ahmed Md Kibria Saroare
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19155v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid growth of large data-center (DC) loads is creating new challenges for power-system visibility, privacy, and cyber-physical security. System operators need accurate short-term information about these fast-varying loads, while DC operators may avoid sharing raw megawatt measurements because they can reveal sensitive workload and utilization patterns. This paper presents FedGuard-DC, a federated learning (FL) framework for privacy-preserving DC load forecasting and local false-data-injection attack (FDIA) detection. Each DC trains a dual-head model on its own measurements, where a shared encoder supports both a forecasting head and a reconstruction head. A calibrated anomaly score combines forecast residual and reconstruction error to detect corrupted measurements locally. Raw measurements and absolute MW demand remain at each DC, while only model updates are shared with the global controller. Optional differential privacy and robust trimmed-mean aggregation are included to evaluate privacy-utility behavior and poisoned-client resilience. The framework is validated using EMT simulation data from four large DC loads rated between 150 and 350 MW integrated into the IEEE 39-bus New England system. Results show a 0.5 s-ahead normalized forecast RMSE of 0.023-0.038 pu, compared with 0.32-0.34 pu for persistence. FedGuard-DC detects FDIA with ROC-AUC of 0.979, F1 = 0.930, and precision of 0.988, while robust aggregation reduces the poisoned-client RMSE impact from 0.042 to 0.035 pu.
tldr: This paper presents a federated learning framework for privacy-preserving load forecasting and cyber-attack detection in data-center loads within power systems.
motivation: The rapid growth of data-center loads challenges power system visibility and privacy, and operators need accurate forecasting while protecting sensitive data.
method: FedGuard-DC uses a dual-head model with a shared encoder for forecasting and reconstruction, and a calibrated anomaly score for FDIA detection, with optional differential privacy and robust aggregation.
result: The framework achieves low forecast RMSE and high FDIA detection accuracy (ROC-AUC 0.979, F1 0.930) on simulated IEEE 39-bus data.
conclusion: The approach demonstrates effective privacy-preserving forecasting and attack detection, but it is not aligned with the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: The Structured Totient Preimage Problem: Reconstruction, Collisions, And Cryptographic Implications
authors: Luis Adri\'an Lizama-P\'erez
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19191v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define and study the Structured Totient Preimage (STP) problem as a restricted reconstruction relation with a direct cryptographic motivation. Let [MATH] be distinct primes of the same bit length and reveal only [MATH]. Given [MATH], STP asks for any set of [MATH] distinct [MATH]-bit primes satisfying this product. The relation is efficiently verifiable, but its reconstruction complexity is not known. We establish three concrete results. First, for factored [MATH] we derive the exact number of ordered exponent allocations and a bound showing that direct reconstruction is polynomial for fixed [MATH] when [MATH]; this rules out that regime as a basis for a strong hardness claim. Second, we give exhaustive algorithms for reconstruction and collision analysis. Third, we exhaustively evaluate 28 parameter pairs, with [MATH], up to [MATH] for pairs and 4,588,935 prime sets in the largest census. The data quantify non-injectivity through collision participation, maximum multiplicity, and conditional ambiguity in bits. These results isolate STP from general inverse-totient computation and motivate a Structured Totient Preimage Assumption for explicitly growing parameter families. Under such an assumption, STP becomes a candidate preimage-resistant relation whose implications for commitments, proofs of knowledge of multiplicative witnesses, and authentication can be stated precisely. The paper establishes the computational foundation and parameter constraints for those constructions; it does not claim a security reduction or post-quantum hardness.
tldr: This paper introduces the Structured Totient Preimage (STP) problem, a number-theoretic reconstruction problem with cryptographic implications, but it is not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
motivation: The authors aim to define a new hard problem based on the Euler totient function that could serve as a basis for cryptographic primitives, motivated by the need for preimage-resistant relations.
method: They formalize the STP problem, derive bounds on reconstruction complexity for fixed parameters, and provide exhaustive algorithms and computational experiments for small parameter sets.
result: They show that direct reconstruction is polynomial for fixed k when n is factored, and they quantify non-injectivity through collision statistics across many parameter pairs.
conclusion: The paper establishes the computational foundation for STP and proposes a Structured Totient Preimage Assumption, but does not provide security reductions or post-quantum hardness.

title: Entropy-Constrained Adaptive Stochastic Quantization
authors: Ran Ben Basat, Yaniv Ben-Itzhak, Michael Mitzenmacher, Shay Vargaftik
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18147v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Adaptive stochastic quantization (ASQ) is a recently introduced quantization approach that optimizes the Mean Squared Error (MSE) for a given input while preserving unbiasedness. It is designed to alleviate the communication and memory bottlenecks of modern data and machine learning workloads, including model, gradient, and KV-cache compression and nearest-neighbor search. Further, practical systems can then compress quantized data with a lossless entropy encoder. However, existing unbiased methods, including ASQ, choose their quantization values without considering this later encoding stage, leaving accuracy on the table. We formulate the Entropy Constrained Adaptive Stochastic Quantization (ECASQ) problem, which jointly selects adaptive quantization values to minimize MSE under an entropy budget and an unbiasedness constraint. We give an optimal dynamic program with [MATH] time and [MATH] space for a length-d vector and at most s quantization values, and a GPU-friendly approximate dynamic program with [MATH] time and [MATH] space. The approximation guarantees that the solution has an MSE no larger than the optimal solution that uses one fewer bit of entropy per entry. We also provide an iterative refinement procedure for the approximation solution that, in our experiments, yields near-optimal results while retaining a substantial speed advantage over our solver for the optimal solution.
tldr: This paper introduces a quantization method for data compression that optimizes MSE under an entropy constraint, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, or quantum networks.
motivation: The paper addresses communication and memory bottlenecks in machine learning by improving adaptive stochastic quantization with entropy constraints.
method: It formulates the Entropy Constrained Adaptive Stochastic Quantization (ECASQ) problem and provides optimal and approximate dynamic programming algorithms with guarantees.
result: The proposed methods achieve near-optimal MSE under entropy budgets with significant speed advantages in experiments.
conclusion: The work contributes to classical data compression and machine learning, not to the user's research areas.

title: A Fault-Tolerant Spike-Time Interface For Approximate Agreement In Distributed Neuromorphic Systems
authors: Arman Ferdowsi, Maryam Dehghanchenary, Kevin Tierney, Atakan Aral
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18151v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large neuromorphic systems contain many processing tiles that may replicate a shared control parameter such as a threshold reference. If these copies diverge, identical inputs may be processed under different intended settings. We study how tiles can reduce this disagreement when communication carries only labeled spike times and up to \(f\) sender labels may be Byzantine. A raw event stream cannot supply the one-value-per-sender input required by classical approximate agreement because a faulty sender can remain silent, flood a receiver, or report different times to different receivers. We introduce the Spike-time Interface for Faults, or \SIF, which combines paced epochs, sender attribution, per-label \FirstSpike admission, bounded timing error, and a silence sentinel. For an affine one-spike code, midpoint decoding attains the exact deterministic minimax error \(\rho=\min\{1/2,\omega/L\}\), where \(\omega\) is the residual timing uncertainty and \(L\) is the usable encoding window. \SpikeTrim applies the classical mean-subsequence-reduced (MSR) rule to the sender-indexed decoded values. For \(n\ge3f+1\), it guarantees one-step robust validity, the tight noiseless contraction factor \(f/(n-2f)\) under direct updates, an explicit worst-case asymptotic disagreement bound, and finite recovery after transient agreement-state corruption. A closed-form test determines whether a validated timing budget meets a target disagreement. Simulations illustrate the fault threshold, timing dependence, flooding resistance, and recovery. A controlled spiking classifier experiment shows an association between faster control-state alignment and lower prediction disagreement under a finite maintenance budget.
tldr: This paper introduces a fault-tolerant spike-time interface for approximate agreement in distributed neuromorphic systems, addressing Byzantine faults in spike-based communication.
motivation: Large neuromorphic systems replicate control parameters across tiles, and divergence can cause inconsistent processing. The authors aim to reduce disagreement when communication is limited to labeled spike times and some senders may be Byzantine.
method: They propose the Spike-time Interface for Faults (SIF), combining paced epochs, sender attribution, first-spike admission, bounded timing error, and a silence sentinel. They apply the mean-subsequence-reduced (MSR) rule to decoded values for approximate agreement.
result: For n≥3f+1, the protocol guarantees robust validity, tight contraction factor, and finite recovery. Simulations and a spiking classifier experiment demonstrate fault tolerance and reduced prediction disagreement.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical and practical framework for achieving approximate agreement in neuromorphic systems under Byzantine faults, with implications for distributed control in such architectures.

title: Redakto - The Incognito Tab For LLMs
authors: Saurav Kumar Saha, Tom R\"ohr, Felix Bie{\ss}mann
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18260v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are being increasingly used in everyday applications. A major challenge in the context of LLMs or Artificial Intelligence (AI) in general is to ensure privacy when using them, meaning that personally identifiable information (PII) is removed from any text that enters an LLM. These challenges have become more urgent with novel EU legislation. Uncertainty around LLM usage with respect to privacy concerns in EU countries can be a major blocker for the speed of innovation and transfer from research to applications. Here we present , a tool that can be used for anonymizing text prior to feeding it to an LLM or other downstream text processing. We provide state-of-the-art functionalities for both redaction of PII but also when used for pseudonymization. These functionalities are exposed such that they can easily be used by end-users, through the Redakto web application, and by developers and researchers, via REST APIs and model context protocol (MCP) hooks. The implementation is fully open source, requires modest compute resources, and can be readily deployed on local hardware. In contrast to prior work and in order to better assess the quality of the anonymized texts, we conduct extensive empirical evaluations on textual data from legal and medical domain with respect to both privacy and utility of the redacted texts. Our empirical results demonstrate that the texts anonymized with different redaction strategies achieve utility scores on par with the original texts, suggesting that anonymization with Redakto can be used for LLM tasks without substantial negative impact for the tasks we explored.
tldr: This paper presents Redakto, an open-source tool for anonymizing text before feeding it to LLMs, with empirical evaluations on legal and medical data.
motivation: Privacy concerns with LLMs, especially under EU legislation, necessitate tools to remove PII from text before processing.
method: Redakto provides redaction and pseudonymization functionalities via a web app, REST APIs, and MCP hooks, and is evaluated on legal and medical datasets for privacy and utility.
result: Anonymized texts achieve utility scores on par with original texts, indicating minimal negative impact on downstream LLM tasks.
conclusion: Redakto offers a practical, locally deployable solution for text anonymization, but it is an applied tool without novel information-theoretic or thermodynamic contributions.

title: Nearest Graph Laplacians With Prescribed Connected Components: A Convex Framework For Network Reconstruction
authors: Udit Raj, Sudeepto Bhattacharya, Prince Kanhya
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18128v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the problem of constructing the nearest graph Laplacian matrix to a given Laplacian while enforcing a prescribed connected-component structure. Let the vertex set be partitioned into nonempty disjoint blocks [MATH], and let [MATH] be the matrix of the corresponding block-indicator vectors. The constraint [MATH] ensures that these prescribed indicators lie in the nullspace of the optimized Laplacian [MATH], and hence the associated graph has at least [MATH] connected components. To guarantee exactly the prescribed components, we impose additional block-connectivity constraints on the principal blocks [MATH]. These constraints ensure that each prescribed block induces a connected weighted subgraph. The resulting problem is a convex semidefinite optimization problem with a strictly convex Frobenius-norm objective. We prove existence and uniqueness of the minimizer and show that the optimized Laplacian has exactly the prescribed connected components, with nullspace [MATH]. The framework proposed in this work provides a principled tool for quantifying the minimum structural intervention required to transform a graph-based network into one having a prescribed group-separated structure. Numerical examples, including the Sampson monastery positive-affection network, illustrate the nearest faction-consistent weighted reconstruction and the minimum Laplacian perturbation required to realize the prescribed faction structure.
tldr: This paper proposes a convex optimization framework to find the nearest graph Laplacian with prescribed connected components, applied to network reconstruction.
motivation: The authors aim to quantify the minimum structural intervention needed to transform a given network into one with a specified group-separated structure, which is relevant in social network analysis.
method: They formulate a convex semidefinite program with a Frobenius-norm objective, enforcing nullspace constraints and block-connectivity constraints to ensure exactly the prescribed connected components.
result: They prove existence and uniqueness of the minimizer and demonstrate the method on the Sampson monastery network, showing the nearest faction-consistent weighted reconstruction.
conclusion: The framework provides a principled tool for network reconstruction with prescribed connectivity, but it is not related to quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.

title: Toward Topology-Optimized Foundry PDKs: A Seeded Design Framework For Multimode Interferometers
authors: Jacob M. Hiesener, Archana Kaushalram, Joshua J. Wong, Robert P. Pesch, Stephen E. Ralph
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18308v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an end-to-end design methodology for multimode interferometer (MMI)-based photonic devices that combines parameter optimization (PO) on analytical models with seeded topology optimization (TO) to maximize performance while preserving foundry design-rule compliance. A PO seed device is further refined via seeded TO, accessing a larger design space than analytical or parameterized methods alone can reach. We validate this pipeline on a 1x2 splitter, a TE modal multiplexer, and a polarization splitter, fabricating and measuring the first two on a commercial foundry process. Seeded TO reduces the measured insertion loss of the 1x2 splitter from 0.20 to 0.14 dB and improves TE00 transmission of the modal multiplexer from -2.79 to -1.01 dB over O-band. Applying this pipeline to a commercial foundry process design kit (PDK)-provided 1x2 and 2x2 splitter improves simulated transmission and tightens the 2x2 splitting ratio from 0.524 to 0.506, along with improved fabrication robustness, offering a practical, foundry-validated route toward incorporating TO-designed components into commercial PDKs.
tldr: This paper presents a design methodology for multimode interferometers using parameter optimization and seeded topology optimization, validated on a commercial foundry process.
motivation: The authors aim to improve the performance of photonic devices while maintaining foundry design-rule compliance, addressing the gap between analytical design and full topology optimization.
method: They combine parameter optimization on analytical models with seeded topology optimization, then fabricate and measure devices on a commercial foundry process.
result: Seeded TO reduces insertion loss of a 1x2 splitter from 0.20 to 0.14 dB and improves TE00 transmission of a modal multiplexer from -2.79 to -1.01 dB, with improved splitting ratio and fabrication robustness.
conclusion: The pipeline offers a practical route to incorporate topology-optimized components into commercial PDKs, enhancing performance while preserving manufacturability.

title: Directional Hydrogen Migration In Acetonitrile Dication In Asymmetric Ultrashort Intense Laser Fields
authors: Sato Miyasaka, Yuki Ono, Hiroka Hasegawa, Runa Kuroda, Akitaka Matsuda, Akiyoshi Hishikawa
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18393v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate intramolecular hydrogen migration in acetonitrile dication in phase-controlled [MATH]-[MATH] intense laser fields (800 and 400 nm, 3.3[MATH]10[MATH] W/cm[MATH]) using three-dimensional coincidence ion momentum imaging. The two-body Coulomb explosion pathway, CH[MATH]CN[MATH] [MATH] CH[MATH] + CN[MATH], exhibits a clear phase-dependent fragment asymmetry along the laser polarization direction, showing that the tunnel ionization preferentially prepares the acetonitrile dication with the methyl group pointing toward the smaller amplitude side of the laser electric fields. The Coulomb explosion pathway occurring after the migration of a single hydrogen atom, CH[MATH]CN[MATH] [MATH] CH[MATH] + HCN[MATH], shows a pronounced reduction in the fragment asymmetry. A clear deuteration effect observed for the asymmetry of the hydrogen-migration pathway suggests that the two-color asymmetric laser field has a significant impact on directionality of intramolecular hydrogen migration in acetonitrile dication.
tldr: This paper studies directional hydrogen migration in acetonitrile dications driven by asymmetric two-color intense laser fields, using coincidence ion momentum imaging.
motivation: Understanding and controlling intramolecular hydrogen migration in molecules under intense laser fields is important for femtochemistry and controlling chemical reactions.
method: The authors used phase-controlled 800 nm and 400 nm intense laser fields to ionize acetonitrile, and employed three-dimensional coincidence ion momentum imaging to measure fragment asymmetries from Coulomb explosion pathways.
result: They observed a clear phase-dependent asymmetry for the two-body pathway, and a reduced asymmetry for the hydrogen-migration pathway, with a deuteration effect indicating the laser field influences migration directionality.
conclusion: The asymmetric laser field can control the directionality of hydrogen migration in acetonitrile dications, offering a means to steer molecular dynamics.

title: Branching (Almost) Everywhere And All At Once
authors: Alyssa Ney
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18644v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is sometimes said that a reason to prefer Everettian quantum mechanics is that it allows one to avoid the kind of spooky action at a distance that is a consequence of quantum entanglement according to other approaches. There is a straightforward argument to show EQM has this virtue, however some advocates argue that this requires we see branching as a local causal process. I explain this reasoning and then show why, given the way Everettians standardly conceive of worlds and branching as emergent phenomena, branching need not be viewed as a causal process for EQM to be relativistically local. Forthcoming in Local Quantum Mechanics, OUP 2026.
tldr: This paper discusses the locality of branching in Everettian quantum mechanics, arguing that branching need not be viewed as a causal process for the theory to be relativistic local.
motivation: The author aims to address a common argument that Everettian quantum mechanics avoids nonlocality, and to clarify the role of branching in this context.
method: The paper provides a conceptual analysis of Everettian quantum mechanics, examining the standard conception of worlds and branching as emergent phenomena.
result: The author concludes that branching does not need to be considered a causal process for EQM to be relativistically local.
conclusion: The paper offers a philosophical clarification of locality in Everettian quantum mechanics, but does not present new technical results in quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Comparative Study Of Nonperturbative Electron-positron Pair Production By Intense Laser Fields Colliding With Either Bremsstrahlung $\gamma$-rays Or Relativistic Ions
authors: S. Remme, A. B. Voitkiv, S. Villalba-Ch\'avez, C. M\"uller
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18718v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is well known that electron-positron pairs can be created in the strong-field environments formed by (i) a high-intensity laser field and a high-energy [MATH]-photon (nonlinear Breit-Wheeler process) or (ii) a high-intensity laser field and a nuclear Coulomb field (nonlinear Bethe-Heitler process). Both of these processes are particularly interesting in the interaction regime where the laser field enters nonperturbatively. Various experimental collaborations are currently aiming at detecting for the first time the nonperturbative Breit-Wheeler process, by exploiting high-intensity laser pulses and [MATH]-ray sources based on bremsstrahlung. In contrast, an experimental observation of the nonlinear, nonperturbative Bethe-Heitler process still lies further ahead in the future because its technical realization appears at present more challenging. Our comparative study shows, however, that the physical properties of the total rates for the processes (i) and (ii) can become remarkably similar when the parameters for the bremsstrahlung-driven nonperturbative Breit-Wheeler process are properly chosen. In this sense, the upcoming experiments on the nonlinear Breit-Wheeler process could also be used to closely ``simulate'' the currently hard to observe nonlinear Bethe-Heitler process.
tldr: This paper compares nonperturbative electron-positron pair production via laser fields colliding with bremsstrahlung gamma-rays or relativistic ions, showing similar rates under certain conditions.
motivation: To understand and potentially simulate the nonlinear Bethe-Heitler process using the more accessible nonlinear Breit-Wheeler process in upcoming experiments.
method: The authors perform a comparative theoretical study of the total rates for the two processes, adjusting parameters to match conditions.
result: They find that the physical properties of the total rates become remarkably similar when parameters are properly chosen.
conclusion: Upcoming experiments on nonlinear Breit-Wheeler could serve as a proxy to study the nonlinear Bethe-Heitler process.

title: Electron Correlation Enables Phase-Coherent One-Attosecond Pulse Trains
authors: Andr\'es Marchisio, Isobel Mcsweeney, Paraskevas Tzallas, Maciej Lewenstein, Marcelo F. Ciappina
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18773v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Attosecond synthesis is ultimately a phase problem: a broad spectrum produces an ultrashort waveform only if its harmonics remain phase-locked. We show theoretically that correlated two-electron high-harmonic generation in helium driven by a long, multicycle laser pulse supports a train of soft-x-ray bursts with durations approaching 1 as. Using a two-electron strong-field approximation, we calculate the complex harmonic spectrum and reconstruct the temporal emission while retaining its full intrinsic spectral phase, rather than imposing a flat-phase approximation. Despite the trajectory-dependent phase accumulated by two continuum electrons, the correlation-extended plateau contains a broad phase-coherent region reaching the keV range. Its superposition produces reproducible bursts separated by one half-cycle of the driving field. These results identify electron correlation not only as a mechanism for extending the high-harmonic cutoff, but also as a route toward phase-coherent x-ray waveforms on the zeptosecond timescale.
tldr: This paper theoretically demonstrates that electron correlation in helium high-harmonic generation can produce phase-coherent one-attosecond pulse trains, extending the cutoff to the keV range.
motivation: Attosecond pulse synthesis is limited by phase coherence; the authors explore whether electron correlation can provide a new mechanism for generating ultra-short, phase-locked x-ray pulses.
method: Using a two-electron strong-field approximation, they calculate the complex harmonic spectrum and reconstruct temporal emission while retaining the intrinsic spectral phase.
result: They find a broad phase-coherent region in the correlation-extended plateau, producing reproducible bursts separated by half-cycle of the driving field, with durations approaching 1 as.
conclusion: Electron correlation is identified as a route toward phase-coherent x-ray waveforms on the zeptosecond timescale, potentially enabling new ultrafast sources.

title: $Ab$ $initio$ Calculation Of Hyperfine-structure Properties To Extract Nuclear Magnetic Octupole Moments Of $^{69}$Ga And $^{71}$Ga
authors: Fei-Chen Li (school Of Physics And Advanced Energy, Henan University Of Technology, Zhengzhou, China), Yong-Bo Tang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We calculate the hyperfine-structure properties of the low-lying states in [MATH]Ga and [MATH]Ga using the relativistic coupled-cluster method at the singles and doubles (RCCSD) level. The properties include the first-order hyperfine constants and the second-order corrections arising from off-diagonal hyperfine interactions. Based on our theoretical results, we reanalyze the previous hyperfine-splitting measurements of the [MATH] state in [MATH]Ga [R. T. Daly and J. H. Holloway, Phys. Rev. 96, 539 (1954)], and refine the nuclear magnetic octupole moments of these two isotopes. The refined values [MATH] and [MATH] are about 13\% and 12\% larger than the earlier results reported by Daly and Holloway. By providing the first independent determination, the present results offer a reliable set of reference values for the magnetic octupole moments of [MATH]Ga, which will benefit both future high-precision measurements and nuclear-structure calculations.
tldr: This paper calculates hyperfine-structure properties of Gallium isotopes to refine nuclear magnetic octupole moments, which is a nuclear physics/atomic physics topic unrelated to the user's research interests.
motivation: The user's research interests focus on quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum systems. This paper is about atomic and nuclear structure calculations, which do not align with any of these directions.
method: The authors use the relativistic coupled-cluster method at the singles and doubles level (RCCSD) to compute hyperfine constants and second-order corrections.
result: They refine the nuclear magnetic octupole moments of 69Ga and 71Ga, finding values about 13% and 12% larger than previous measurements.
conclusion: The refined values provide a reliable reference for future high-precision measurements and nuclear-structure calculations, but the work is not relevant to the user's research areas.

title: Toward Realistic Energy Forecasting: A Delay-Enhanced Fractional-Order Supply-Demand Model
authors: S. Noeiaghdam S. Naveen
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18121v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In order to represent the complex dynamics of contemporary energy systems, a novel fractional-order energy supply-demand model with time delay is presented in this investigation. The fractional model, compared to traditional integer-order models, naturally accommodates for memory and genetic effects, and the incorporation of delay component takes into account unavoidable lags in energy production, transmission, and consumption. To ensure the mathematical rigor of the proposed model, we prove the existence and uniqueness of solutions. We additionally examine into the model's stability within the Ulam-Hyers concept and demonstrate that it is resilient to minor uncertainties and perturbations. To handle fractional derivatives with delay systems, we utilize the Grnwald-Letnikov (GL) discretization scheme, which offers a straightforward and effective method for approximating the solutions. The impact of delay parameters and fractional orders on system behavior is investigated numerically, demonstrating how they shape oscillations, convergence rates, and equilibrium states. According to the results, fractional-order modeling with delay, reinforced by the GL discretization scheme, provides a flexible and realistic framework for examining energy dynamics. This framework gives important insights for long-term policy planning, supply management, and demand forecasting. Additionally, the framework lays the groundwork for upcoming additions that incorporate optimization techniques, stochastic effects, and the integration of renewable energy sources, all of which will further the development of effective and sustainable energy systems. We also discuss three sensitivity analysis scenarios including high demand combined with low supply, high renewable and reduced and imports low demand with high imports which the results show stable and efficient results.
tldr: This paper proposes a fractional-order energy supply-demand model with time delay for realistic energy forecasting, focusing on mathematical stability and numerical simulations.
motivation: Traditional integer-order models fail to capture memory and genetic effects in energy systems, and delays in production/transmission/consumption are often ignored. The authors aim to provide a more realistic framework for energy dynamics.
method: They introduce a fractional-order differential equation model with time delay, prove existence/uniqueness of solutions, analyze Ulam-Hyers stability, and use the Grünwald-Letnikov discretization scheme for numerical approximation.
result: Numerical simulations show that fractional order and delay parameters influence oscillations, convergence rates, and equilibrium states. Sensitivity analysis under three scenarios yields stable and efficient results.
conclusion: The fractional-order delay model offers a flexible and realistic framework for energy forecasting and policy planning, with potential extensions to optimization, stochastic effects, and renewable integration.

title: Learning The Center And Radius Of Wasserstein Ambiguity Sets For Data-Driven Decision Making
authors: Junjie Guo
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18123v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization (DRO) is commonly built around the empirical distribution, with the ambiguity radius selected from a concentration bound. Although this construction provides useful statistical guarantees, it can be conservative and does not fully exploit predictive information about the underlying distribution or the difficulty of a particular decision problem. We develop a more flexible framework in which a predictive model determines the nominal distribution and a separate model estimates a data-dependent radius. The key requirement is not that the ambiguity set be centered at the empirical distribution, but that it contain the unknown data-generating distribution with the desired probability. We establish finite-sample guarantees and asymptotic consistency for arbitrary learned centers, derive tractable reformulations for non-uniform discrete predictive distributions, separate predictive-model and scenario-discretization errors, and prove stability under simultaneous perturbations of the center and radius. We further characterize the oracle conditional-quantile radius as the smallest conditionally valid rule and introduce a split-conformal procedure for finite-sample marginal calibration. Experiments on newsvendor problems, synthetic portfolios, distribution shifts, and real financial data show that learned and calibrated ambiguity sets can improve reliability, but do not automatically yield smaller radii or better decisions. Overall, the proposed framework treats calibration as a practical mechanism for reliable decision making rather than a universal guarantee of improved optimization performance.
tldr: This paper proposes a data-driven framework for learning the center and radius of Wasserstein ambiguity sets in distributionally robust optimization, with statistical guarantees and calibration.
motivation: Standard Wasserstein DRO uses the empirical distribution and a concentration-bound radius, which can be conservative and ignores predictive information. The authors aim to improve reliability by learning both the center and radius from data.
method: They develop a framework where a predictive model determines the nominal distribution and a separate model estimates a data-dependent radius, ensuring the ambiguity set contains the true distribution with high probability. They provide finite-sample guarantees, tractable reformulations, and a split-conformal calibration procedure.
result: Experiments on newsvendor and portfolio problems show that learned and calibrated ambiguity sets can improve reliability, but do not automatically yield smaller radii or better decisions.
conclusion: The framework treats calibration as a practical mechanism for reliable decision making, not a universal guarantee of improved optimization performance.

title: Optimizing Energy Efficiency And Grid Stability Via Public Ev Charging Flexibility
authors: Marek Miltner, Artem Bryksa, Ond\v{r}ej \v{s}togl, Daniel Va\v{s}ata, Magda Friedjungov\'a, Ram Rajagopal, Old\v{r}ich Star\'y
abstract: ArXiv:2608.18126v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study evaluates the potential of electric vehicle (EV) charging flexibility to enhance both energy efficiency and power grid stability. Using real-world data from public charging stations in Prague, we analyze individual and aggregated charging sessions to explore how optimizing charging times can reduce energy waste, minimize grid imbalances, and support the integration of renewable energy. By aligning EV charging with periods of lower grid demand and higher renewable generation, we demonstrate a significant improvement in energy efficiency, reduc ing the need for costly system support and ancillary services. Our findings suggest that cooperation between power distributors and transmission system operators can unlock new opportunities for maintaining grid stability while promoting sustainable energy use in an increasingly uncertain energy landscape.
